second_track.conclusion: The 6 detections fall into 3 fixed sky positions, each seen only within < 4 h (too short for the static-source flag); a polynomial of order 2 passes through 3 points exactly, so the fit says nothing about motion. A straight line through the same points has rms 4.0" (chi2_red 29) versus 1.4" for the quadratic. Position 0 (201.39257, -8.12068; 1 member(s)): a single-exposure event in 2025W25_1B_0290_3 D6 at 4.94 um (S/N 19.0); its peak pixel stands 4.5x higher above its neighbours than a PSF-sampled source would, the other exposures of the same visit on the same detector (minutes apart) give forced S/N [0.13, 0.47, 0.46], the simultaneous exposure on the other detector gives [-1.09], and nothing is catalogued there: most likely an unflagged cosmic-ray or detector hit. Catalogue sources within 6": gaia_dr3 0, 2mass_psc 0, allwise 0, SIMBAD 0. Position 1 (201.38873, -8.12191; 2 member(s)): a STATIC source: forced S/N stacks to 14.9 over 19 exposures below 2.42 um (median 3.5) but 1.1 above; it crosses 5 sigma only in 2 exposure(s). Catalogue sources within 6": gaia_dr3 1, 2mass_psc 0, allwise 1, SIMBAD 0. Position 2 (201.37214, -8.11009; 3 member(s)): a STATIC source: forced S/N stacks to 15.1 over 19 exposures below 2.42 um (median 3.8) but 3.4 above; it crosses 5 sigma only in 3 exposure(s). Catalogue sources within 6": gaia_dr3 1, 2mass_psc 0, allwise 1, SIMBAD 0. sb_ident from SPHEREx (positive control finds Kleopatra: True) lists [7, 8, 8, 11, 11, 11] known bodies within 0.1 deg of the members, the nearest 100" away (none within the 12" match radius). The geocentric (code 500) lookup used in motion_check.json finds Kleopatra at its own position: True. Most likely explanation: NOT a moving object, but two faint static sources (each with a Gaia DR3 and an AllWISE counterpart) that reach 5 sigma only in a few short-wavelength exposures, plus one single-exposure artefact; the order-2 fit through three positions made them look like a slow track.
